newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan opposition cut off north of Kabul -- Taleba.
newsitem.headline: Afghan opposition cut off north of Kabul -- Taleba.

text.p: Afghan Taleban fighters said on Tuesday they had taken a key piece of high ground overlooking rival territory, contradicting opposition claims.

"We have taken the high ground overlooking the villages of Qaloqan and Mir Batcha Kot (17 miles - 27 km north of Kabul). Their forces cannot move along the road any more," a Taleban commander a short way behind the front lines told reporters.
A spokesman in the opposition stronghold of Mazar-i-Sharif said on Tuesday their forces had repulsed three Taleban attacks in the past 24 hours without losing any territory.
"Each time our forces beat them back and we did not lose any ground, the Taleban forces suffered heavy casualties in the attacks," said the spokesman.

The Taleban fighters did not allow journalists to visit the front line itself to verify their claims, saying it was too dangerous, but they said there had been no change apart from the capture of the high ground.
At its closest point the front line is still some 12 miles (20 km) from Kabul, putting the city within rocketing range of the opposition.
In a rapid advance towards Kabul last week the opposition punched a salient towards Kabul, but then the advance stopped, leaving the opposition exposed to Taleban artillery and rocket batteries.
If it is confirmed, the Taleban's claim to have captured the high ground is the first movement since last Friday.

The Taleban forces are dug in at the same place where they stopped an opposition advance last October. But analysts in Kabul say there has been a change in the relative strengths of the warring factions since then.
